findings.description: Account balances are modified before ledger.record() is invoked. If ledger.record raises ValueError, the function propagates the exception without rolling back the account changes, violating the contract.
findings.evidence: When transfer is called with memo length > 40, lines 18-19 decrement accounts[src] and increment accounts[dst], then line 20 calls ledger.record which raises ValueError at line 7. The spec explicitly requires that any raised ValueError leaves both accounts and the ledger entirely unchanged.

review.summary: The transfer function violates the contract's atomicity requirement by mutating account balances before calling ledger.record(). If ledger.record raises ValueError (e.g., for a memo longer than 40 characters), accounts will already be modified, contradicting the requirement that a raised ValueError must leave both accounts and the ledger entirely unchanged.
